transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, uh, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place for this. Um, I guess I'm just here because... well, things have been a little different lately. My father-in-law moved in with us recently, and, you know, it's an adjustment for everyone. I'm an EMT, so I'm used to handling stressful situations, and I'm still doing fine at work, really. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. 

But, um, at home and with my bachelor's coursework, I've just been a little more... wound up, I guess? Maybe a bit shorter with people than I usually am. And I haven't been doing my usual hobbies—like fishing, woodworking, or even the first-aid workshops I usually help out with. I just haven't had the energy for them. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this right.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge more often than usual lately?

Anxious? Um... no, I wouldn't really use that word. I mean, I'm an EMT, so I'm pretty good at keeping a level head, you know? I definitely don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. 

I wouldn't say I'm on edge or anxious... just, maybe a little distracted? Or tired? With my father-in-law in the house and my classes, it's just a really full plate right now. But definitely not anxious. Is it okay that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you been feeling sad or down more often than usual lately?

Sad? Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. Um, I have a lot to be thankful for, really. I definitely don't want to come across like I'm complaining or feeling sorry for myself. 

I'm really not down in the dumps or anything like that. I think it's just... well, like I was saying, maybe just a bit worn out from the new routine at home. I hope it's helpful that I can rule that out for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Enjoying them? Um... yeah, absolutely. I still really love all that stuff. 

Like I mentioned earlier, I just haven't really had the time or... well, the energy to actually get out and do them. But the interest is definitely still there. I mean, if things were a little less hectic at the house right now, I'd be out fishing or in the woodshop in a heartbeat. It's just that with everything going on, I need to focus on my family and my classes, which I think is the responsible thing to do, you know? 

So, yes, I definitely still enjoy them. I hope that answers your question okay? I really don't want to give you the impression that I'm losing interest in things or giving up on what I like.
Are you having trouble feeling pleasure when you do think about or engage in the activities you normally enjoy?

Pleasure? Oh, yeah, for sure. When I actually get a minute to think about getting back out on the water, or, you know, working on a project in the shop... it still sounds great. 

I wouldn't say I'm having trouble feeling pleasure at all. It's really just the time factor right now. If I could actually get out there, I know I'd have a great time. I definitely don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling miserable or anything like that. I'm just doing what I have to do right now for my family. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Sleeping? Um, no, no trouble there. I actually sleep pretty well. 

I mean, once my head hits the pillow, I'm usually out for the night. I might wake up a few minutes early here and there, just, you know, mentally running through my to-do list for my classes or what the family needs that day, but nothing I'd call trouble. I definitely get plenty of rest. 

I hope that's a good sign? I want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture, but yeah, I'm definitely not lying awake all night or anything like that. Is that helpful?
Have you been wanting to be around friends or family less often than you used to?

Less often? Um, no, not at all. I actually really enjoy being around everyone. 

Like I mentioned, I'm spending most of my time right now focusing on my family anyway, just trying to be there for them. I definitely haven't been pulling away or, you know, avoiding my friends either. I'd hate for you to think I'm isolating myself, because I know that's probably not a good thing to do. I still really value my connection with people, especially with my background as an EMT, you know, I'm used to being around folks and helping out. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how things are going. I'm definitely still a people person, I promise.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?

Appetite? Oh, no, no changes there. I'm eating just fine. 

I mean, working as an EMT for so long, you kind of learn early on that you have to eat and keep your energy up, so I've always been pretty good about my meals. Even with everything going on and focusing on the family right now, I make sure I sit down and eat properly. 

I definitely wouldn't want you to worry that I'm skipping meals or not taking care of myself, because I'm really staying on top of all that. I'm healthy in that department. I hope that's the kind of information you need? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for.
Do you feel like you have less energy than you used to?

Energy? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I feel like my energy is actually pretty good. 

I mean, I'm fifty-one now, so maybe I don't have the exact same bounce I did in my twenties, but I'm definitely not dragging or anything. I still get up and tackle the day, take care of the family, keep up with my classes... I'd really hate for you to think I'm just sort of sitting around on the couch letting things slide, because I'm definitely staying active and getting things done. 

I hope that's reassuring? I just want to make sure you know I'm still functioning well and keeping my stamina up. Does that answer what you were looking for?
Have you been looking forward to social events or gatherings?

Social events? Oh, definitely. I still really look forward to them. 

Like, if a friend invites me over or there's a family thing, I'm absolutely there. I haven't been, you know, making excuses or trying to get out of things. I'd hate to give the impression that I'm becoming antisocial or anything like that, because I really do enjoy getting together with people. It's good to catch up and just be around everyone. 

I hope that sounds okay? I just want to be clear that I'm still very much engaged and enjoying the things I usually do. Is that the kind of thing you were wondering about?
Do you find yourself thinking about your hobbies, such as fishing or woodworking, less often than you used to?

Hobbies? Oh, well... I mean, I still think about them. I haven't completely forgotten about them or anything. 

It's just that, well, I came in today because things have been a little... different lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have been a bit of an adjustment. I'm still completely holding it together at work, absolutely no issues there. But at home, and with my coursework, I guess I've been a little more wound up and short-tempered than I usually am. I really don't want you to think I'm losing control or anything, it's just a bit more stressful right now. 

And because of that, I guess I have started skipping the fishing and woodworking... and even those first-aid workshops I usually go to. They normally help keep my head clear, but I've just been so focused on the family. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just giving up on the things I love? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by prioritizing my family right now. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way, with the adjustments and stress at home?

It's been... well, about four months now. Basically right since my father-in-law moved into our house. 

I really thought I'd have the new routine completely mastered by now, you know? Especially with my line of work, I'm usually so good at managing situations and keeping everyone calm. But four months isn't actually that long of a time to adjust to a whole new living situation, right? I'd hate for you to think I'm just letting this drag on or not trying to adapt. I'm definitely working hard on getting us all settled and making sure he's comfortable. 

I hope that sounds like a reasonable amount of time to still be figuring things out? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the way I should be, and that I'm not overreacting. Does that timeframe seem normal to you?
Do you still think about planning or doing your hobbies like fishing or woodworking even when you're not actually doing them?

Well, I... I do still think about them, yes. I haven't just erased them from my mind or anything like that. 

Like, if I walk past the garage and see my tools, or if it's a nice weekend and I know the fish are biting, I'll definitely think, "Oh, it would be great to get out there." I'm still very interested in those things. I just... I haven't been acting on those thoughts as much lately, because of everything going on at home. I don't want you to think I've lost my passion for them, because I really haven't. It's just a temporary pause, you know? 

I hope it's okay that I'm still thinking about them even if I'm not doing them right now? I just want to make sure I'm keeping a healthy mindset about it all. Does that sound like a normal way to handle a break from your hobbies?
Do you still feel motivated to start new projects related to your hobbies, such as beginning a new woodworking task?

Start something new? Um... well, to be completely honest, not really. I haven't exactly felt the push to go out and buy new lumber or draw up plans for a fresh project lately. 

But it's not like I'm just sitting around doing nothing! I just figure... with the house being so busy right now, it wouldn't be very considerate of me to start tearing up the garage and leaving sawdust everywhere. I'm really just trying to be responsible and not add to the chaos, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I've completely lost my spark. I just think holding off on big new projects is the best way to keep the peace at home right now while we're all still adjusting. That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm just trying to do what's best for everyone, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just letting myself go.
Do you still enjoy spending time with your friends and family as much as you used to?

Well, I... I definitely still love my friends and family. That hasn't changed at all. I mean, family is everything, right? 

I guess I haven't been seeing my buddies quite as much lately. Usually we'd grab a beer or watch a game, but I've been turning down a few invitations. It's not that I don't want to see them, it's just... I feel like I need to be around the house more right now, with my father-in-law there. I want to make sure my wife feels supported, and it wouldn't look great if I was just taking off to hang out with the guys while she's managing things at home. 

And when we do have family dinners, I'm still there, of course! I might be a little quieter than usual, just because my mind is kind of preoccupied with making sure everyone else is doing okay. But I'm still enjoying the time together. I really don't want you to think I'm isolating myself or pushing people away. I'm just trying to be a supportive husband and son-in-law right now. 

That's a pretty normal reaction when your family needs you, isn't it? I hope I'm doing the right thing by putting them first.
Do you still find yourself looking forward to the idea of doing your hobbies like fishing or woodworking in the future?

Well, yeah, absolutely. I definitely still look forward to getting back to them. I mean, I think about the spring and getting the boat out, or finally finishing that coffee table I was thinking about a while back. 

I just... I see it as something down the road, you know? Once things settle down here with my father-in-law and we find a good rhythm, I'll be right back out there. I really want to make sure I'm prioritizing my family right now, so pushing those things to the future just feels like the responsible choice. 

I'm not giving up on the things I love, I promise. It's good to have things to look forward to, right? That shows I'm still keeping a positive outlook on things, doesn't it?
Do you still initiate conversations with friends and family, or do you mostly respond when they talk to you?

Oh, um... I guess I haven't really kept track of who starts the talking, to be honest. I'd like to think I still reach out! I mean, I'll still shoot a text to the guys or ask my wife how her day went. 

Maybe... maybe lately I've been a little more on the listening end of things? Just because, you know, with the situation at home, sometimes it's just easier to let them steer the conversation. I really try to be a good listener for my wife right now, especially with her dad living with us. That's important, right? Being a supportive ear? 

I definitely don't want it to seem like I'm withdrawing or ignoring anyone. I just... I guess I don't want to make every conversation about the stress at the house, so I let them take the lead and talk about their day instead. I figure nobody wants to hear me complain, and it's better to just be there for them. That's a pretty normal way to handle things, don't you think? I'm just trying to be considerate.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?

Well, I wouldn't say I've *lost interest* exactly. I mean, I still think fishing and woodworking are great, and I usually love going to those first-aid workshops... they've always been how I keep my head clear, you know? 

It's just that lately, ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have been a bit... stretched. I'm holding it together at work just fine—I'm an EMT, so I have to be on my game there—but when I get home, or when I try to focus on my coursework, I'm just a little more wound up and short-tempered than I'm used to being. 

So, I guess I have been skipping the workshops and the hobbies for now. Not because I don't like them anymore! Just... I feel like I need to use that time to keep things running at home. It's just a temporary thing, prioritizing family over my own downtime. That makes sense, right? It's better to be a little stressed and put those things on hold than to let my family down, don't you think?
For how long have you been feeling less like doing your hobbies such as fishing or woodworking?

Um... let's see. I'd say it's been about four months now? Yeah, right around the time my father-in-law moved in with us. 

But I mean, four months isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? It's just an adjustment period. Anyone would need a little time to get used to having another person in the house, especially someone who needs a bit of extra care. I just figured taking a few months off from my own stuff to focus on the family was the right thing to do. That's a pretty normal timeline for getting settled into a big change like this, isn't it?

I guess I haven't been seeing my buddies quite as much lately. Usually we'd grab a beer or watch a game, but I've been turning down a few invitations. It's not that I don't want to see them, it's just... I feel like I need to be around the house more right now, with my father-in-law there. I want to make sure my wife feels supported, and it wouldn't look great if I was just taking off to hang out with the guys while she's managing things at home. 

And when we do have family dinners, I'm still there, of course! I might be a little quieter than usual, just because my mind is kind of preoccupied with making sure everyone else is doing okay. But I'm still enjoying the time together. I really don't want you to think I'm isolating myself or pushing people away. I'm just trying to be a supportive husband and son-in-law right now. 

That's a pretty normal reaction when your family needs you, isn't it? I hope I'm doing the right thing by putting them first.

Well, yeah, absolutely. I definitely still look forward to getting back to them. I mean, I think about the spring and getting the boat out, or finally finishing that coffee table I was thinking about a while back. 

I just... I see it as something down the road, you know? Once things settle down here with my father-in-law and we find a good rhythm, I'll be right back out there. I really want to make sure I'm prioritizing my family right now, so pushing those things to the future just feels like the responsible choice. 

I'm not giving up on the things I love, I promise. It's good to have things to look forward to, right? That shows I'm still keeping a positive outlook on things, doesn't it?

I really try to be a good listener for my wife right now, especially with her dad living with us. That's important, right? Being a supportive ear? 

I definitely don't want it to seem like I'm withdrawing or ignoring anyone. I just... I guess I don't want to make every conversation about the stress at the house, so I let them take the lead and talk about their day instead. I figure nobody wants to hear me complain, and it's better to just be there for them. That's a pretty normal way to handle things, don't you think? I'm just trying to be considerate.

patient.answer:
Well, I wouldn't say I've *lost interest* exactly. I mean, I still think fishing and woodworking are great, and I usually love going to those first-aid workshops... they've always been how I keep my head clear, you know? 

It's just that lately, ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have been a bit... stretched. I'm holding it together at work just fine—I'm an EMT, so I have to be on my game there—but when I get home, or when I try to focus on my coursework, I'm just a little more wound up and short-tempered than I'm used to being. 

So, I guess I have been skipping the workshops and the hobbies for now. Not because I don't like them anymore! Just... I feel like I need to use that time to keep things running at home. It's just a temporary thing, prioritizing family over my own downtime. That makes sense, right? It's better to be a little stressed and put those things on hold than to let my family down, don't you think?
